title: Building and Fire – Mercantile Occupancy December 2013
description: Owners built three additions to a former low-hazard industrial (F3) building without permits, then applied for a permit without engineered drawings. The building was used for an internet retail business with a walk-in sales floor (roughly 30–70 visitors a day). The building SCO asked for a code review by an architect and a professional engineer.

refusal.basis: not applicable: permit refusal based on occupancy classification (mercantile, not F3); no alternative solution was proposed

outcome_summary: Permit refusal confirmed (major occupancy is Group E mercantile, defined by use, not visitor numbers). The fire order was varied to add evacuation if directives are not met.

quotes.text: The Appeal Panel was not provided with any alternative solutions for their consideration.

The SCO requested a building code review by an architect and a professional engineer. The panel held that 'a safety codes officer is not bound by the judgment of the registered professionals engaged by the Appellants' (in the context of s.49 orders and reclassification).
